commit e524d9f429f9c937ecd2eb9315144a28b3f27090
Author: Dan LaRocque <dalaro@hopcount.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 1 16:34:29 2014 -0400

    Add ConfigNamespace/ConfigOption to titan-hadoop
    
    This commit introduces a ConfigNamespace and several ConfigOptions to
    titan-hadoop and replaces several hardcoded string keys scattered
    around the code with ConfigOption uses.
    
    This is not a complete migration away from Hadoop Configuration.  A
    few of the unresolved issues:
    
    * Hadoop Configuration's setClass(String key, Class impl, Class iface)
      method does not have an exact equivalent in the titan-core
      configuration API.  It could be modeled with ConfigOptions
      parameterized in a composite value representing a pair of impl and
      iface, but that's not ideal.
    
    * Hadoop Configurations are unavoidable when working with MR, so I
      took the approach extending Hadoop's Configured base class with a
      HybridConfigured subclass that maintains both a Hadoop Configuration
      and read-only Titan configuration backed by the Hadoop
      Configuration.  All writes currently have to go though the Hadoop
      Configuration though, and that's cumbersome in some places.
    
    * Several input and output format-specific options haven't been
      migrated to ConfigOption at all (e.g. rdf and edgelist options)

diff --git a/titan-hadoop-parent/titan-hadoop-core/src/main/java/com/thinkaurelius/titan/hadoop/config/TitanHadoopConfiguration.java b/titan-hadoop-parent/titan-hadoop-core/src/main/java/com/thinkaurelius/titan/hadoop/config/TitanHadoopConfiguration.java
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..9b82891fd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/titan-hadoop-parent/titan-hadoop-core/src/main/java/com/thinkaurelius/titan/hadoop/config/TitanHadoopConfiguration.java
@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+package com.thinkaurelius.titan.hadoop.config;
+
+import com.thinkaurelius.titan.diskstorage.configuration.ConfigNamespace;
+import com.thinkaurelius.titan.diskstorage.configuration.ConfigOption;
+
+public class TitanHadoopConfiguration {
+
+    public static final ConfigNamespace ROOT_NS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(null, "h-root", "titan-hadoop configuration root");
+
+    public static final ConfigNamespace TRUNK_NS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(new ConfigNamespace(ROOT_NS, "titan", "titan-hadoop namespace"), "hadoop", "titan-hadoop namespace"); // TODO fix descriptions
+
+    public static final ConfigNamespace INPUT_NS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(TRUNK_NS, "input", "Input format");
+
+    public static final ConfigOption<String> INPUT_FORMAT = new ConfigOption<String>(
+            INPUT_NS, "format",
+            "Package and classname of the input format class.  This must implement the Hadoop InputFormat interface.",
+            ConfigOption.Type.LOCAL, "current");
+
+    public static final ConfigOption<String> INPUT_LOCATION = new ConfigOption<String>(
+            INPUT_NS, "location",
+            "Path to the default input file",
+            ConfigOption.Type.LOCAL, String.class);

commit 1a7499f21deeeed08f77d5dfa793bda0c26e51e0
Author: Dan LaRocque <dalaro@hopcount.org>
Date:   Tue Dec 2 01:15:14 2014 -0500

    Partitioned vertex filtering for TP3 input formats
    
    Added an option to the HBase/Cassandra
    InputFormat<NullWritable,VertexWritable> implementations built for TP3
    that controls the treatment of Titan's partitioned vertices.  By
    default, the presence of a partitioned vertex in the input causes an
    exception.  Setting titanmr.input.filter-partitioned-vertices=true
    instead drops partitioned vertices and any edges incident on
    partitioned vertices, logging each at debug as it is dropped.
    
    This commit also renames several config keys in
    TitanHadoopConfiguration and adds a test of the new partitioned vertex
    filter setting.  The test code is a bit clumsy since I've tried to
    avoid requiring Giraph for the titan-hadoop tests -- this could
    probably be streamlined once TP3's MapReduceGraphComputer is
    implemented.

@@ -4,23 +4,41 @@ import com.thinkaurelius.titan.diskstorage.configuration.*;
 
 public class TitanHadoopConfiguration {
 
+    public static final ConfigNamespace MAPRED_NS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(null, "titanmr", "Titan MapReduce configuration root");
+
+    // ScanJob configuration
+
     public static final ConfigNamespace SCAN_NS =
-            new ConfigNamespace(null, "mrscan", "MapReduce ScanJob configuration root");
+            new ConfigNamespace(MAPRED_NS, "scanjob", "ScanJob configuration");
 
-    public static final ConfigOption<String> JOB_CONFIG_ROOT =
-            new ConfigOption<String>(SCAN_NS, "conf-root",
+    public static final ConfigOption<String> SCAN_JOB_CONFIG_ROOT =
+            new ConfigOption<String>(MAPRED_NS, "conf-root",
                     "A string in the form \"PACKAGE.CLASS#STATICFIELD\" representing the config namespace root to use for the ScanJob",
                     ConfigOption.Type.LOCAL, String.class);
 
-    public static final ConfigNamespace JOB_CONFIG_KEYS =
-            new ConfigNamespace(SCAN_NS, "conf-keys", "ScanJob configuration");
+    public static final ConfigNamespace SCAN_JOB_CONFIG_KEYS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(MAPRED_NS, "conf", "ScanJob configuration");
 
-    public static final ConfigOption<String> JOB_CLASS =
-            new ConfigOption<String>(SCAN_NS, "class",
+    public static final ConfigOption<String> SCAN_JOB_CLASS =
+            new ConfigOption<String>(MAPRED_NS, "class",
                     "A string in the form \"PACKAGE.CLASS\" representing the ScanJob to use.  Must have a no-arg constructor.",
                     ConfigOption.Type.LOCAL, String.class);
 
-    public static final ConfigNamespace TITAN_INPUT_KEYS =
-            new ConfigNamespace(SCAN_NS, "input-conf", "Titan input configuration");
+    // Titan input configuration
+
+    public static final ConfigNamespace INPUT_NS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(MAPRED_NS, "input", "Titan input configuration");
+
+    public static final ConfigNamespace TITAN_INPUT_CONFIG_KEYS =
+            new ConfigNamespace(INPUT_NS, "conf", "Settings to be passed to TitanFactory.open");
+
+    public static final ConfigOption<Boolean> FILTER_PARTITIONED_VERTICES =
+            new ConfigOption<Boolean>(INPUT_NS, "filter-partitioned-vertices",
+                    "True to drop partitioned vertices and relations incident on partitioned vertices when reading " +
+                    "from Titan.  This currently must be true when partitioned vertices are present in the " +
+                    "input; if it is false when a partitioned vertex is encountered, then an exception is thrown.  " +
+                    "This limitation may be lifted in a later version of Titan-Hadoop.",
+                    ConfigOption.Type.LOCAL, false);
 
 }

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: fab0f61a025f824f76980d54c3aa2cfa435a8c79

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the `ConfigElement.getPath(...)` calls that `7546a2336` changed to use the `includeRoot=true` overload. I looked at when `TitanHadoopConfiguration.GRAPH_CONFIG_KEYS` (used in the fix) was introduced — it was renamed from `TITAN_INPUT_CONFIG_KEYS` in commit `fab0f61a0` ("Bulkloader and Hadoop IO format config key changes"). That same commit also introduced the `getPath(element, boolean includeRoot, ...)` overload. I then examined `ModifiableHadoopConfiguration.java`, which contains the counterpart *read* logic (`prefixView`/`getTitanGraphConf`) used to reconstruct the Titan graph configuration back out of the Hadoop `Configuration` object that the writer classes populate.

**(2) The specific change:** In `fab0f61a0`, the diff to `ModifiableHadoopConfiguration.java` shows:
```
- HadoopConfiguration prefixConf = new HadoopConfiguration(mc.getHadoopConfiguration(), ConfigElement.getPath(prefixRoot) + ".");
+ HadoopConfiguration prefixConf = new HadoopConfiguration(mc.getHadoopConfiguration(),
+         ConfigElement.getPath(prefixRoot, true) + ".");
```
This changed the **read side** to expect keys prefixed with the full namespace path including the root element name (e.g. `titanmr.ioformat.conf.*`). However, the same commit renamed `TITAN_INPUT_CONFIG_KEYS` to `GRAPH_CONFIG_KEYS` in the **write-side** call sites (`MapReduceIndexJobs.java`, `MapReduceIndexManagement.java`, `CassandraHadoopScanRunner.java`, `HBaseHadoopScanRunner.java`, `CassandraScanJobIT.java`) without also switching them to the new `includeRoot=true` overload — they kept calling plain `ConfigElement.getPath(TitanHadoopConfiguration.GRAPH_CONFIG_KEYS)`, which excludes the root name (producing `ioformat.conf.*` instead of `titanmr.ioformat.conf.*`).

This created a mismatch: writers stored config under `ioformat.conf.*` / `scanjob.conf.*` while the reader (`prefixView`) looked for `titanmr.ioformat.conf.*` / `titanmr.scanjob.conf.*`, so the scanjob/index-management helper classes could no longer find their configuration values — exactly the failure that `7546a2336` describes and fixes by adding `, true` to all the remaining write-side call sites.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** `git show fab0f61a0 -- .../ModifiableHadoopConfiguration.java` confirms the read-side behavior change (adding `includeRoot=true`) was introduced there, while `git show fab0f61a0 -- .../MapReduceIndexJobs.java .../MapReduceIndexManagement.java .../scan/CassandraHadoopScanRunner.java .../scan/HBaseHadoopScanRunner.java` confirms those files were touched in the same commit (renaming `TITAN_INPUT_CONFIG_KEYS`→`GRAPH_CONFIG_KEYS`) but left using the old (root-excluding) `getPath` form. `7546a2336` subsequently updates exactly these same files, adding the missing `true` argument, which is a direct, symmetrical fix to the inconsistency introduced in `fab0f61a0`. No intervening commits between `fab0f61a0` and `7546a2336` touch this logic (only an unrelated TP3 upgrade).

I'm confident in this attribution; the read/write symmetry makes the causal chain very clear, with no significant remaining uncertainty.
